subject.title: [Bug] Incomplete environment variable isolation in untrusted Crabbox bootstrap

question: Should untrusted Crabbox execution defend against a hostile inherited runner environment in addition to fork-controlled files and CI-only forwarded variables, and which launcher owns that sanitization?
rationale: The answer determines whether this is an exploitable boundary bypass, defense-in-depth hardening, or an out-of-scope trusted-runner condition; shell-local unsets and global child allowlisting protect different boundaries.

options.title: Prove then harden launcher
options.body: Require a current proof of attacker-controlled inheritance, then sanitize the earliest trusted launch environment and add focused regression coverage.

options.title: Adopt defense in depth
options.body: Treat the runner environment as potentially hostile and introduce an explicit minimal environment contract without requiring a forwarding bypass.

options.title: Keep runner environment trusted
options.body: Document the trusted clean-runner boundary and close unless a bypass of CI-only forwarding is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Prove then harden launcher
recommendation.body: Require a current proof of attacker-controlled inheritance, then sanitize the earliest trusted launch environment and add focused regression coverage.
